questions.q: What is the most common underlying cause of recurring bank statement errors?
options: Genuinely corrupted files sent by the bank
Setup gaps, such as missing accounts or unmapped codes
Oracle's inability to read any text file format
Bank statements never actually fail to load
questions.explain: The large majority of recurring errors trace back to setup gaps rather than genuinely bad files from the bank.

questions.q: What does an 'out-of-balance' statement error indicate?
options: The statement was loaded on the wrong day
The bank account's currency was changed
The account has too many transaction codes
The sum of transaction lines doesn't reconcile to the stated opening and closing balances
questions.explain: An out-of-balance statement means the lines don't sum correctly to the file's own stated balances — a sign of a corrupted file or parsing problem.

questions.q: Why is it risky to simply re-run the Load process on a file after fixing a mapping issue, without checking the prior attempt's state?
options: It can create a duplicate statement if the original attempt already created header/line records
Load can only ever be run once per bank account, permanently
It will automatically delete the bank account
It has no risk at all
questions.explain: If the original attempt already created statement records, rerunning Load without voiding/removing them first can create a duplicate statement.

questions.q: What is the correct general order of the correction workflow described in this lesson?
options: Reprocess immediately, then identify the error afterward
Delete the bank account, then investigate
Identify the error, classify it, fix the root cause, then reprocess
Contact the bank first in every single case, regardless of the error
questions.explain: The workflow is to identify the error, classify it as one-time or recurring, fix the root cause, and only then reload or reprocess.

questions.q: Why does fixing a setup gap 'once' matter more than patching individual statements?
options: Because Oracle only allows one correction per calendar year
Because a setup-level fix prevents the same error from recurring on every future statement
Because patching individual statements is actually the recommended best practice
Because setup gaps cannot be fixed at all
questions.explain: A root-cause fix (like adding a missing mapping) resolves the issue for every future statement, not just the one currently stuck.
